AGENTS.md:
# moke-meta-hackathon

Use pnpm and Vite+. Run pnpm verify before handing back implementation changes.
Project decisions and source provenance live in .project-kit/manifest.json.

## Effect and coding standards

Read repos/effect/LLMS.md before writing Effect code. The matching source, tests,
and ai-docs are read-only references. Import from installed packages, never repos/.
If references were skipped, run project-kit references after committing changes.

Use the installed coding-standards skill. Parse external input with Effect
Schema. Keep known failures typed, use application services and Layers, and make
runtime ownership and cleanup explicit. Generic and Effect anti-slop rules are
vendored in tools/oxlint/anti-slop; preserve local customizations when updating.

## Svelte and design

Use SvelteKit 3 configuration in vite.config.ts, Svelte 5 runes, and #lib imports.
Use the Svelte coding skills and run their autofixer when editing components.

The initial notes UI is a functional smoke example. Choose visual design during
app design from any entry in sc-frederick/uiverse-templates, the user's private
backup of downloaded Uiverse design systems. Forge and Aether are recent choices.
Run project-kit designs to list the archive and project-kit design <slug> to
import the chosen reference. Preserve its DESIGN.md, assets, and license. Keep
reference source outside public distributions and adapt the selected design to
the application rather than adding a second UI system.

## Runtime boundaries

Use Effect SQL and Effect RPC. Web bindings come from the Alchemy declaration;
keep request resources scoped to the request. Desktop database access stays
outside the renderer, with RPC restricted to the app's trusted top-level frame.

Keep SQLite migrations immutable after application. Desktop migrations run after
a consistent backup and stop visibly on failure. Read docs/data.md before changing
migration or recovery behavior. Read docs/deployment.md before release changes.

Authentication and cloud capabilities are selected per application. Implement
authorization at operation boundaries. Choose desktop updater delivery and access
per project; aecPermitMonitor is a reference to evaluate for R2-hosted updates.

Scaffolding itself does not deploy resources or publish applications. Follow the
user's requested scope when moving from local implementation to external changes.
README.md:
# moke-meta-hackathon

Generated with project-kit: pnpm, Vite+, SvelteKit 3, Effect 4, Effect SQL,
Effect RPC, native TypeScript 7 checking, and vendored anti-slop rules.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm effect:setup
pnpm dev
```

The desktop UI is packaged inside Electron. The web UI uses Alchemy's SvelteKit
Worker integration with a stage-isolated D1 database. Check docs/deployment.md
for the applicable environment and credential setup.

## Verification

```sh
pnpm exec playwright install chromium
pnpm verify
project-kit doctor .
```

Tests include real SQLite persistence and one UI/RPC/database smoke flow. The
web smoke flow uses local Miniflare D1 and needs no Cloudflare credentials.
Desktop smoke tests launch Electron and need a graphical session or Xvfb on Linux.
TypeScript 6 supplies APIs used by Svelte tooling; TypeScript 7 performs native
checking. Vite+ runs format, lint, and native checks; svelte-check --tsgo covers
Svelte components. Re-run pnpm effect:setup after dependency installation to
restore Effect diagnostics in the native compiler.

## Project choices

Choose authentication before deployment. The default is undecided. Authenticated
apps must implement and pass test:auth before deployment. Apps intentionally
without login record authentication as none in .project-kit/manifest.json.

Choose visual design later from the private Uiverse archive with project-kit
designs and project-kit design <slug> . . Adapt the selected reference into the
Svelte UI, keeping its source assets and license out of public template releases.

## Maintenance

```sh
project-kit update .
git apply --stat .project-kit/update.patch
project-kit update . --apply
pnpm install
pnpm effect:setup
pnpm verify
```

Updates use the original scaffold as the three-way merge base. Local edits are
preserved and conflicts stop application. Review the diff and commit it. If the
Effect dependency changed, run project-kit references after committing, then
commit the updated subtree provenance. Never edit applied database migrations.
docs/data.md:
# Data lifecycle

Application queries use Effect SQL. Parse rows with Effect Schema before returning
domain values. Do not assume D1 supports the same transaction APIs as local SQLite;
use its atomic batch primitive for fixed multi-statement operations.

## Desktop

The database is app.sqlite in Electron's userData directory. Startup closes its
migration connection before acquiring the application SQL Layer. The Node SQLite
driver uses the built-in node:sqlite module, so no separate native SQLite addon is
required. Heavy database work can move to a utility process when the app needs it.

Add migration files named 0001_name.sql, 0002_name.sql, and so on. Files may contain
multiple SQL statements. The runner owns transactions; migrations must not contain
transaction control statements. It verifies hashes of previously applied files,
backs up the database using SQLite's consistent backup API, then applies pending
files and history records in one transaction. Failures preserve existing data.
The five most recent automatic pre-migration backups are retained.

File > Export database creates a consistent backup, including committed WAL data.
File > Restore database checks integrity and migration compatibility, closes the
application runtime, keeps a pre-restore backup, replaces the database, and
restarts. A migration or restore failure must never reset or delete user data.

## Web

Alchemy owns D1 provisioning and migration application through the migrations
property in alchemy.run.ts. Commit reviewed SQL before deploying. Do not run a
second migration tracker through Wrangler or an application startup hook. Separate
statements inside a web migration file with `--> statement-breakpoint`, which the
local smoke runner and Alchemy migration parser both recognize.

Development, staging, and production have separate databases. Set up an explicit
export/restore procedure before destructive production schema changes. Schema
changes must remain compatible with the currently deployed app during rollout;
an app rollback does not reverse a database migration.

## Sync

Cloud connectivity is optional. Decide the source of truth, offline writes,
conflict rules, idempotency keys, deletions, and compatibility with older desktop
clients for the particular application. RPC provides transport and contracts;
it does not supply synchronization semantics.

import { resolve } from "node:path";

// Keep the registered rules explicit so application type checking never traverses
// the vendored plugin implementation. Review this list when its upstream pin moves.
const genericRules = [
  "no-array-filter-map",
  "no-reduce-accumulator-copy",
  "no-chained-type-assertions",
  "no-conditional-empty-object-spread",
  "no-known-value-widening",
  "no-module-mocking",
  "no-object-parameters",
  "no-reflect-apply",
  "no-reflect-get",
  "no-runtime-typeof",
  "no-unsafe-dictionary-type",
  "no-shape-in-symbol-names",
  "no-unknown-parameters",
  "no-unknown-returns",
  "no-unknown-type-aliases",
  "no-widen-then-assert",
  "require-readable-spacing",
  "require-safety-comment-for-type-assertion",
];

const effectRules = [
  "no-manual-effect-error-tag",
  "no-manual-tag-comparison",
  "no-manual-tagged-construction",
  "no-service-constructor-imports",
  "prefer-effect-match",
];

/** Enable the pinned generic and Effect rules from the vendored plugins. */
export function lintSettings(pluginDirectory = "tools/oxlint/anti-slop") {
  return {
    options: { typeAware: true, typeCheck: true },
    ignorePatterns: [
      "repos/**",
      "tools/oxlint/**",
      "node_modules/**",
      ".svelte-kit/**",
      "build/**",
      "dist/**",
      "release/**",
      ".alchemy/**",
      ".wrangler/**",
      "test-results/**",
      ".project-kit/**",
      "design/reference/**",
      ".agents/**",
      ".codex/**",
      ".claude/**",
    ],
    jsPlugins: [
      { name: "anti-slop", specifier: resolve(pluginDirectory, "index.ts") },
      { name: "anti-slop-effect", specifier: resolve(pluginDirectory, "effect/index.ts") },
    ],
    rules: {
      "oxc/no-accumulating-spread": "error" as const,
      ...Object.fromEntries(genericRules.map((name) => [`anti-slop/${name}`, "error" as const])),
      ...Object.fromEntries(
        effectRules.map((name) => [`anti-slop-effect/${name}`, "error" as const]),
      ),
    },
  };
}

import { RuleTester } from "oxlint/plugins-dev";

import { noArrayFilterMapRule } from "./no-array-filter-map.ts";

const tester = new RuleTester({ languageOptions: { parserOptions: { lang: "ts" } } });
const error = { messageId: "arrayFilterMap" };

tester.run("anti-slop/no-array-filter-map", noArrayFilterMapRule, {
  valid: [
    "const users = []; users.values().filter(active).map(email).toArray();",
    "const users = []; users.values().map(email).filter(Boolean).toArray();",
    "Iterator.from(users).filter(active).map(email).toArray();",
    "function collect(users: IteratorObject<User>) { return users.filter(active).map(email).toArray(); }",
    "const users = []; users.flatMap(user => user.active ? [user.email] : []);",
    "const users = []; users.map(email); users.filter(active);",
    "const users = []; users.map(email).map(normalize);",
    "const users = []; users.filter(active).filter(verified);",
    "const custom = { filter() { return this; }, map() {} }; custom.filter(active).map(email);",
    "function collect(unknownReceiver) { return unknownReceiver.filter(active).map(email); }",
    "const users = fetchUsers(); users.filter(active).map(email);",
    "const users = []; function collect(users) { return users.filter(active).map(email); }",
    "let users = []; users = iterator; users.filter(active).map(email);",
    "const users = []; users[method](active).map(email);",
    "const first = second; const second = first; first.filter(active).map(email);",
  ],
  invalid: [

    { code: "function collect(users: ReadonlyArray<User>) { return users.filter(active).map(email); }", errors: [error] },
    { code: "function collect(users: Array<User>) { return users.filter(active).map(email); }", errors: [error] },
    { code: "const users = [] as const; users['filter'](active)['map'](email);", errors: [error] },

The rule is MIT-licensed. Keep `LICENSE` with every redistributed copy, including skill assets. No Stylistic, ESLint, TypeScript-ESLint, or additional parser runtime dependency is required.

## Local adaptations

- Replace upstream type aliases with Oxlint's ESTree, context, token/comment, and rule types. Upstream's token type includes comments; Oxlint exposes those separately.
- Replace `AST_NODE_TYPES` enum members with identical string literals.
- Guard indexed reads for consuming repositories with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. Impossible missing AST/configuration entries raise explicit invariant errors rather than introducing new non-null assertions.
- Replace the repository-specific `createRule` factory with `createPaddingLineRule(options, statementTypes?)`. The anti-slop wrapper supplies typed options directly; it exposes no user configuration options. The optional second argument registers caller-defined statement types, consulted before the upstream table, so a policy can match syntax the upstream matchers do not distinguish (exported bindings, comment ownership) without editing the vendored tables.
- Implement the small required AST helper surface in `padding-line-ast.ts` using Oxlint's public source-code/token API. `isParenthesized` only needs the one-pair check used to exclude parenthesized directive strings, not the upstream general-purpose overloads.
- Retain the upstream statement matchers, scope tracking, comment-aware insertion/removal, selector support, and diagnostic text. Upstream naming and non-null assumptions remain localized here to keep future diffs reviewable; the file is not a model for new application code.

The opinionated policy lives outside this directory in `../../rules/require-readable-spacing.ts`. It adds spacing without collapsing existing blank lines. Short local bindings, consecutive imports, and adjacent overload signatures/implementation remain grouped. Spacing is syntactic, not an inference of business-logic boundaries.

## Updating and verification

Fetch an explicit upstream revision, compare the original rule and types against this revision, and port relevant fixes while retaining the adapters above. Update this record and preserve the license. Run `pnpm check` and `pnpm sync:skill-assets` as required by repository guidance.

Focused Oxlint RuleTester cases live in `../../rules/require-readable-spacing.test.ts`; they test exact fixes, JSDoc/trailing comments, same-line statements, semicolon-free code, TypeScript exports/overloads, Effect-style generators, and upstream removal behavior. `../../rules/require-readable-spacing-cli.test.ts` verifies the exported plugin through the native Oxlint CLI on multiple files, including rejection, autofix, and repeated-fix stability. The complete upstream JS/TS test suites have not been ported; this is focused compatibility evidence, not a claim of full upstream conformance.

name: Verify desktop
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  verify:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, windows-2025, macos-15]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm effect:setup
      - run: pnpm check
      - run: pnpm test
      - run: pnpm build
      - if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: xvfb-run -a pnpm test:e2e
      - if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        run: pnpm test:e2e
      - run: pnpm exec electron-builder --dir --publish never
        env:
          CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: "false"
.github/workflows/release.yml:
name: Unsigned desktop release
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, windows-2025, macos-15]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: Verify tag matches package version
        shell: bash
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: node -e 'const p=require("./package.json"); if (process.env.RELEASE_TAG !== `v${p.version}`) process.exit(1)'
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm effect:setup
      - run: pnpm check
      - run: pnpm test
      - run: pnpm build
      - if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: xvfb-run -a pnpm test:e2e
      - if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        run: pnpm test:e2e
      - run: pnpm exec electron-builder --publish never
        env:
          CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: "false"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: desktop-${{ runner.os }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          path: |
            release/*.exe
            release/*.dmg
            release/*.zip
            release/*.AppImage
            release/*.deb
            release/*.blockmap
            release/*.yml
  publish:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: artifacts
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Hash release artifacts
        working-directory: artifacts
        run: find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum > SHA256SUMS
      - name: Publish release artifacts
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          gh release create "$RELEASE_TAG" artifacts/* --repo "$REPOSITORY" --verify-tag --generate-notes
docs/deployment.md:
# Desktop releases

Development uses a loopback Vite server. Release builds package a static SvelteKit
3 application in Electron with the same schema-first Effect RPC contract, carried
over MessagePorts. The preload bridge exposes only the application's RPC endpoint.
The main process authorizes the trusted top-level frame before connecting it.

GitHub CI checks and packages Windows, macOS, and Linux builds. Releases run from
version tags matching package.json. They publish unsigned installers and SHA256SUMS
to GitHub Releases after all builds succeed. Code signing and notarization are not
configured; the workflow does not require Apple or Windows developer credentials.
Unsigned applications retain the platform's normal installation prompts.

```sh
pnpm package:desktop
```

Increment package.json's version, commit the release, then push its matching v tag
when ready to publish. The generator itself never creates release tags.
The initial homepage assumes `sc-frederick/<project-name>`; update package.json to
the actual project URL before release. Linux desktopName and application identity
are generated from the project name.

## Update delivery

Choose the updater and download access for each application. The user often hosts
release files on R2 and presents notices, downloads, and installation inside the
app. Evaluate aecPermitMonitor's implementation before reusing it. The baseline
does not hardcode a bucket, feed, public-download policy, or universal installer.

An updater must select the matching OS/architecture artifact, verify it before
execution, report progress and failure, preserve data, and distinguish download,
installation, and restart. Test its behavior with the actual unsigned artifacts.
Some platform updater paths require signing; use an installer handoff or manual
replacement where automatic installation is unavailable. Do not promise a uniform
silent update path across unsigned Windows, macOS, and Linux distributions.

## Data, configuration, and logs

The main process owns SQLite and filesystem access. File > Export database and
File > Restore database provide data recovery. Read docs/data.md before changing
that lifecycle. Never add database or filesystem capabilities directly to the UI.

Logs are JSON lines in userData/logs, one file per date. Use Effect Redacted for
secrets and avoid logging user data or credentials. Hosted monitoring is optional.
Store persistent credentials through the OS credential facility; never bundle
provider API tokens or store them in renderer localStorage.

Cloud features are optional. Add Cloudflare + Alchemy with development, staging,
and production separation when required. Authentication, sync ownership, offline
behavior, and conflict policy are chosen for the application.

macOS artifacts receive an ad-hoc signature on the runner, which requires no
Apple developer account. They have no Developer ID signature or notarization,
so Gatekeeper can still require an explicit user override. Windows artifacts
have no publisher signature.
